newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay shares stage upward break out.
newsitem.headline: Cathay shares stage upward break out.

text.p: Hong Kong's flag carrier Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd soared to a new high on Friday on good earnings growth forecasts and derivatives-generated interest, brokers said.

The share blasted to an all-time high of HK$16.35, confirming its breakout from a four-year trading range with an upside barrier of HK$15.00. The share then eased to trade up HK$0.25 at HK$15.90 in early afternoon.

"Recent research reports have suggested the share is worth HK$20.00, based on the airline's earnings outlook after the new airport opens," said Tim Ip, director of trading of financial products at CEF Capital Ltd.
"It is a high growth stock and cheaper than SIA (Singapore International Airlines )," said said Ip.

Hong Kong's new international airport is scheduled to open in April 1998. While landing costs and other fees are likely to be much higher than at present, the 24-hour airport will allow Cathay to increase and improve its routes, in particular its service to Europe.
Other brokers said demand was generated by three recent issues of covered warrants on the stock.
Canadian Imperial Bank of Canada issued 150 million American-style call warrants on Cathay on Thursday, close on the heels of an issue by Indosuez W.I. Carr of 170 million warrants.
The CIBC warrants were issued at a premium of 14.2 percent and with a gearing of 4.13 times and the Indosuez WICO warrants had a premium of 15.34 percent and a gearing of 4.92 times.
Bear Sterns Inc issued 210 million call warrants on Cathay on June 18. That issue was put out with a premium of 14.95 percent and with a gearing of 5.01 times.
"We were approached...to issue covered warrants on certain stocks," said Alistair Candlish, managing director, Indosuez W.I. Carr Derivatives.
Most of the demand for these covered warrants came from individuals investors, said Candlish
"Hong Kong has turned back into a retail market," he said emphatically. "We think the current momentum (of the market) will carry on for the next five to six weeks."
Another broker said demand for covered warrants varied from issue to issue and said the Cathay warrants were sought by both retail and institutional investors.
